definitions.explanation: A dignified sense of pride or self-respect, especially the kind maintained by professionals, craftspeople, or people of principle. A more literary and elevated word than {誇|ほこ}り.

examples.japanese: ⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{矜持|きょうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: To have pride as a craftsperson.

examples.japanese: {矜持|きょうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捨|す}てて→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧⟦{頭|あたま}を{下|さ}げる→頭を下げる：26795_atamawosageru⟧こと⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦できなかった→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: I could not throw away my pride and bow my head.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦{培|つちか}って→培う：07926_tsuchikau⟧きた⟦{料理人|りょうりにん}→料理人：19396_ryourinin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{矜持|きょうじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{妥協|だきょう}→妥協：07423_dakyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{許|ゆる}さなかった→許す：02325_yurusu⟧。
examples.english: The professional pride cultivated over many years as a chef would not allow any compromise.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary and formal word for pride. Unlike ⟦{誇|ほこ}り→誇り：03623_hokori⟧ (general pride) or ⟦プライド→プライド：22290_puraido⟧ (personal pride, often ego-driven), {矜持|きょうじ} carries a nuance of dignified self-respect rooted in one's profession, principles, or identity. Often used about professionals and craftspeople.

Also read きんじ in some contexts, though きょうじ is the standard modern reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {矜持|きょうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧: to have pride/dignity
- {矜持|きょうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧: to protect one's dignity
- {矜持|きょうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捨|す}てる→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧: to abandon one's pride
- ⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{矜持|きょうじ}: a craftsperson's professional pride
